title: CS-SE alignment cadence prep — strategic account (Keira Morgan)
content:
Purpose:
- Prep notes for sync with SE (Diego) ahead of account QBR next month. Align on risks, deployment plan, and win criteria.

Context / quick history: (short)
- Customer: TitanRetail (pilot started Jan 2025).
- Prod footprint: 2 models (chat+embeddings) on Dedicated beta (reserved pool).
- Last quarter: increased latency incidents when seq len spikes during peak demand (Mar-May). Engineering patch rolled Apr 10, but still seeing intermittent spikes tied to weekend batch jobs.
- Commercial: ARR expansion potential but decision deferred pending SLO confirmation and cost predictability.

Meeting goals (top 3):
1) Agree on immediate mitigation priority list for next 2 weeks (who owns what).
2) Get SE commitment on a tech checklist we can show the customer before QBR (latency dashboard + predicted cost impact).
3) Draft shared ask document for customer execs (two options: conservative vs aggressive rollout).

Draft agenda (30–40 min):
- 00-05m: quick context + current open incidents (me)
- 05-12m: Diego summarizes SE investigation & root cause hypotheses
- 12-22m: Agree on mitigation runbook (hotfix vs config change vs reroute) and owners
- 22-30m: Customer-facing artifacts we need (dashboards, one-pager, cost delta scenarios)
- 30-35m: Risks, escalation path, confirm next steps and who will communicate what to customer

Signals to pull before meeting (prep actions):
- Attach latest latency heatmap (alerts from Observability) — Nina to grab (open ticket)
- Cost delta calc: run sim of batching + prefix caching (approx monthly delta) — Diego to run quick sim on staging
- Recent error traces grouped by model and time-of-day (SLO breaches) — me (Keira) to export

Hypotheses to test / call-outs to discuss:
- H1: Weekend batch job causes cache thrashing -> spikes. If true, temporary schedule shift reduces incidents by ~60%.
- H2: Model variant (non-quantized) in routing for certain routes causes higher GPU memory pressure -> spikes. Possible short-term: fallback to smaller variant.
- H3: Autoscaler cooldown too short -> oscillation on scale-up/down (investigate scaling metrics).

Key probing questions for Diego (SE):
- Which of the three hypotheses has telemetry supporting it today? (ask for specific traces/links)
- How fast can we test schedule shift vs fallback variant in staging? CI/CD blockers?
- What config changes on Dedicated would be non-disruptive (no credential rotation)?
- Can we produce a 1-slide technical summary that non-engineers can digest for the QBR?

Customer-facing artifacts we should produce (MVP list):
- 1-page incident summary + mitigation plan (conservative, aggressive).
- Latency SLO dashboard view (90/95/99 p99) + historical trend for last 90 days.
- Cost sensitivity table: current vs with aggressive caching + quantization (monthly delta).

Draft action items (owner — due):
- Export and annotate top 5 traces showing cache thrash pattern — Keira — 2025-07-20
- Run batching/prefix-cache cost sims (two configs) and drop numbers in shared sheet — Diego — 2025-07-21
- Build one-slide tech summary for QBR (layman's bullets + 1 chart) — Liam — 2025-07-24
- Create 1-page incident + mitigation doc (draft) — Keira + Nina — 2025-07-23
- Confirm runbook for temporary routing fallback (playbook steps) — Diego — 2025-07-22

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep customer language simple — avoid kernel/quantization jargon; use "model variant" and "performance profile".
- Customer exec cares about predictability and cost first — prioritize cost scenarios.
- There is a contract clause about performance credits — flag legal if we propose credits.

Escalation path (quick):
- If p99>1.5s for >2 hours during business day -> immediate page to oncall SRE and SE lead (Diego).
- For >=3 repeated incidents in 7 days -> scheduled emergency meeting with customer + EM from serving runtime.

Unresolved / open questions (to resolve in meeting):
- Can we get temporary additional burst capacity for Dedicated pool for a weekend test? (billing/ops constraint)
- Will model quantization materially degrade accuracy for their reranking flow? Need example prompts to test.

Slack snippets (copy/paste-ready):
- To SE channel: "Heads up — prepping alignment sync for TitanRetail QBR. Need quick sim on batching + prefix-cache by Tue (Diego). Can you confirm feasibility?"
- To PM: "Want to show a simple graph of p99 over 90 days in QBR. Nina and I will pull the data; can you help with slide slot?"

Prep checklist (before meeting):
- [ ] attach latency heatmap
- [ ] attach top traces
- [ ] have cost sim notes inline in sheet
- [ ] confirm Diego availability and runbook draft ready

Meeting logistics:
- Proposed length: 35 min
- Mode: Zoom (record) + create meeting notes doc (this doc will be source-of-truth)

Quick follow-ups to send immediately after meeting (templates):
- Short summary + agreed action list (email to customer leads) — Keira to send within 24h
- Internal playbook update (add whatever we decide about fallback routing) — Diego to PR to repo

Misc scratch: 
- If customer wants to push to private (on-prem) because of data, note added infra complexity and longer lead time -> flag in QBR options.
- Keep a short 'what success looks like' line for QBR: "p99 < target AND predictable monthly cost within 10% of estimate"

---
Last minute TODO: double-check SLO target in contract (legal clause 5b) — if different, call out in slide.

End of notes.
